originalQuestion: Are eggs good to eat, bad to eat, or best in moderation, and how does the answer vary across people?
compiledQuestion: For a 31-year-old resistance-trained man, does replacing his current breakfast with two whole eggs six days per week improve body composition over twelve weeks without materially worsening cardiometabolic risk?
decisionContext: I am 31, male, live in Muttichur, Kerala, and do weight training six days a week. I can buy twelve eggs from a local farmer next week and realistically eat two with breakfast on training days. I care about body fat, strength, energy, sleep, resting heart rate, cost, and whether the available eggs create a material safety tradeoff. The farmer does not provide detailed feed or certification records.
knownUnknowns: Baseline LDL and ApoB are not supplied
The farmer's feed and certification are unknown
The exact current breakfast comparator is incompletely specified
